meta.experiment: Experiment 06 — Flight Performance: Thrust-to-Weight, Hover Throttle, Control Margin & Payload
meta.note: Flight-performance database. Thrust and mass are kept in grams-force / grams so the thrust-to-weight ratio is dimensionless (g cancels). Prop diameters in metres, power in watts. The default combo (2204 motor, 620 g/motor) on the 500 g reference airframe reproduces every worked example in theory.md: TWR = 4.96, hover throttle 44.9%, max payload 740 g, hover efficiency 11.36 g/W. The empty mass is inherited from Experiment 2 and the motor from Experiment 1.

config.note: Quadcopter: total max static thrust = motor_count x max_thrust_per_motor. Payload adds to the inherited empty mass and lowers the TWR.

propulsion.label: 1806 2300KV + 5" (4S)
propulsion.note: Light 5-inch build. Modest thrust; good for an efficient cruiser.

propulsion.label: 2204 2300KV + 5" (4S)
propulsion.note: Reference 5-inch freestyle propulsion. 4 x 620 g on a 500 g frame gives TWR 4.96 and a 44.9% hover throttle.

propulsion.label: 2207 1600KV + 5" (6S)
propulsion.note: High-power 6S racer. Very high TWR (~8) for explosive acceleration.

propulsion.label: 2212 920KV + 10" (4S)
propulsion.note: Large slow-turning prop. High disk area -> efficient hover; good lifter.

propulsion.label: 2808 1200KV + 7" (6S)
propulsion.note: 7-inch long-range / freestyle. Strong thrust with a moderately large disk.

propulsion.label: 3508 700KV + 13" (6S)
propulsion.note: Heavy-lift / cinematic. Big 13-inch disk gives the best hover efficiency (g/W).

propulsion.label: 4008 380KV + 15" (6S)
propulsion.note: Large cinelifter motor. Very large 15-inch disk — high thrust and excellent hover efficiency.

propulsion.label: 5010 280KV + 16" (6S)
propulsion.note: Industrial heavy-lift. 16-inch disk for maximum payload capacity at low disk loading.

twr.description: Thrust-to-weight ratio: total static thrust divided by weight. Both in grams-force, so g cancels: TWR = N x T_max / m_total.
twr.note: A drone needs TWR > 1 just to leave the ground and >= 2 for controllable flight with manoeuvre headroom. Reference build: 4 x 620 / 500 = 4.96 (freestyle).

hover.description: At hover each motor must produce one quarter of the weight. With the quadratic propeller thrust curve (T proportional to throttle^2, because T proportional to RPM^2 and RPM proportional to throttle) the hover throttle is the square root of the thrust fraction.
hover.note: Hovering near 50% throttle is ideal: it leaves symmetric authority to push up and ease down. Reference build hovers at 44.9% (55.1% margin).

payload.description: The extra mass the craft can carry while keeping a minimum safe thrust-to-weight ratio for controllable flight.
payload.note: Reference build: m_max = 4 x 620 / 2 = 1240 g, payload = 1240 - 500 = 740 g. Loading payload raises total mass and drives TWR down toward the limit.

efficiency.description: Ideal hover power from momentum (actuator-disk) theory, divided by the figure of merit for real-rotor losses. Efficiency is the lift produced per watt.
efficiency.note: Reference build: A = 0.0507 m^2, P_hover = 44.0 W, efficiency = 11.36 g/W. Larger props (bigger disk area) hover far more efficiently; a heavier craft is less efficient because P grows as thrust^1.5.

connections.note: Empty mass is inherited from the Experiment-2 build and the motor from the Experiment-1 propulsion design, so the performance envelope reflects the actual aircraft assembled across the lab series.

constants.note: Standard gravity. Shared across all experiments.
